claims.text: What an EKG measures An EKG records the heart's electrical activity from the body surface. Each lead views the heart from a different angle, and the size and direction of each deflection reflect the net depolarization or repolarization vector relative to that lead.
claims.quote: An electrocardiogram records the electrical activity of the heart from the body's surface. Each lead views the heart from a different angle, producing a unique tracing. The size and direction of each deflection reflect the net vector of electrical depolarization or repolarization relative to that lead's axis.

claims.text: The leads Limb leads (frontal plane): bipolar I, II, III; augmented aVR, aVL, aVF
claims.quote: Limb leads (frontal plane): Bipolar leads: I, II, III Augmented leads: aVR, aVL, aVF

claims.text: Precordial leads (horizontal plane): V1 through V6
claims.quote: Precordial leads (horizontal plane): V1 through V6

claims.text: Lead groups → region → usual artery Inferior: II, III, aVF → RCA (80%) or LCx
claims.quote: Inferior II, III, aVF RCA (80%) or LCx

claims.text: Lateral: I, aVL, V5, V6 → LCx or diagonal
claims.quote: Lateral I, aVL, V5, V6 LCx or diagonal

claims.text: Posterior: mirror-image changes in V1–V3 → RCA or LCx
claims.quote: Posterior Mirror in V1–V3 RCA or LCx
